Definition: from G1909 and G3007; to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for:--fail.
BiblicalUsage: Epileipo means to fail, to be insufficient — and the writer of Hebrews says, what shall I more say, for the time would fail me to tell of Gideon, and Barak, and Samson, and Jephthae, of David also, and Samuel, and of the prophets.
TheologicalSignificance: The failing of time is the highest praise, I hold: the stories of faith are too many to tell, and the list runs out before the faith does.
